common: Hellebore Ice N' Roses Early Rose
visual: Robust clump-forming hellebore with leathery dark green palmate foliage and large outward-facing rich rose-pink flowers with prominent yellow stamens, flowering through winter into spring.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist but never permanently saturated.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained neutral to alkaline soil.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and very dry exposed ground.
prune: Remove damaged or old foliage before flowering and deadhead after flowering if seed is not required.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten and sap may irritate skin; wear gloves when handling.
cvs: Coseh 4000 (HGC Ice N' Roses Early Rose)
hardinessNote: Below −20°C · exceptionally hardy in UK conditions.
resilience: Very cold-hardy, robust and long-lived; tolerates more sun than many traditional hellebores if soil remains adequately moist.
uses: Winter borders, woodland edges, underplanting, wildlife gardens, patio containers, cut flowers.

visual: Bushy late-season chrysanthemum producing masses of warm bronze to rusty orange-red daisy-like flowerheads above aromatic divided green foliage.
water: Moderate to high while actively growing and flowering; do not allow container plants to dry completely.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging; container-grown plants require reliable drainage.
prune: Deadhead regularly to prolong flowering and cut back stems after flowering or once growth dies down.
toxicity: May cause skin irritation in sensitive people; wear gloves when handling extensively.
hardinessNote: Hardiness depends on the exact cultivar sold under this name; some autumn pot chrysanthemums require winter protection.
resilience: Good late-season flowering performance but exact winter resilience depends strongly on cultivar and drainage.
uses: Autumn containers, seasonal displays, sunny borders, pollinator planting.
uncertain: The supplied name 'AUTUMN BRONZE' is insufficient to determine the exact commercial chrysanthemum clone.
Chrysanthemum 'Autumn Bronze' is an established cultivar name, but UK nursery material may instead refer to Poppins Autumn Bronze or Chrysanthemum 'Prelude Autumn Bronze'.
A photograph of the original label would allow the cultivar and hardiness rating to be narrowed down.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with dark young stems and small glossy grey-green leaves edged creamy white, developing attractive pink and crimson tones in colder weather.
water: Moderate while establishing; water container-grown specimens regularly during dry weather.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained soil of most normal pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground and very exposed frost pockets.
prune: Trim lightly in spring or summer to maintain shape; ball-trained plants can be clipped regularly during the growing season.
hardinessNote: −10 to −5°C · hardy through much of the UK but benefits from shelter in colder inland gardens.
resilience: Good wind and coastal tolerance once established, although severe frost can damage young growth.
uses: Topiary balls, containers, evergreen structure, coastal gardens, low hedging, mixed borders.
uncertain: The word 'Ball' describes the nursery-trained topiary form and is not part of the cultivar name.

visual: Tall, substantial yarrow with aromatic fern-like grey-green foliage and broad, flat clusters of rich red to burgundy flowers on strong upright stems.
water: Low to moderate; water while establishing, then allow soil to dry somewhat between watering.
soil: Well-drained soil of almost any normal pH.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently wet or rich, heavily fertilised soil, which can encourage weak floppy growth.
prune: Deadhead regularly to extend flowering and cut old stems back after flowering or in late winter.
toxicity: May cause skin irritation in sensitive people; ingestion can cause digestive upset.
resilience: Highly drought and heat tolerant once established and performs well in exposed sunny planting.
uses: Prairie planting, cottage borders, wildlife gardens, cut flowers, drought-tolerant schemes.
uncertain: The supplied word 'Choice' appears to be nursery or label wording rather than part of the cultivar name.

visual: Large upright evergreen shrub with glossy dark green serrated foliage and fragrant semi-double peony-form rose-pink flowers opening in late autumn and winter.
water: Moderate; maintain consistent moisture, particularly during establishment and summer when flower buds are forming.
soil: Acidic, organic-rich, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or strongly chalky soil and cold waterlogged ground.
prune: Usually requires little pruning; shape immediately after flowering if necessary.
hardinessNote: −10 to −5°C · hardy through much of the UK in a sheltered position.
resilience: Evergreen and robust once established but flower buds and young growth benefit from protection from cold drying winds.
uses: Woodland gardens, wall-side borders, evergreen screening, specimen shrub, large containers.

visual: Compact yarrow with finely divided grey-green foliage and sturdy branching stems carrying dense flattened clusters of rich red flowers that soften in colour as they age.
water: Low to moderate; water while establishing but avoid constant wetness.
soil: Well-drained soil of most normal textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and excessive feeding.
prune: Deadhead frequently to prolong flowering; cut stems back after flowering or leave seedheads until late winter.
toxicity: May irritate sensitive skin and can cause digestive upset if eaten in quantity.
resilience: Cold-hardy, drought tolerant once established and tolerant of exposed sunny sites.
uses: Borders, prairie planting, wildlife gardens, cut flowers, containers.

visual: Compact clump-forming Japanese anemone with toothed mid-green leaves and distinctive ruffled semi-double white flowers flushed soft lilac around golden-yellow centres.
water: Moderate; prefers consistently moist soil, especially during active growth and flowering.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged drought and stagnant waterlogged soil.
prune: Cut flowered stems back after flowering and remove old foliage as it dies down.
toxicity: Potentially harmful if eaten and sap may irritate skin.
resilience: Very cold-hardy once established and tolerant of both sun and partial shade where soil retains moisture.
uses: Mixed borders, cottage gardens, woodland edges, containers, late-season planting.

visual: Compact bushy catmint with aromatic soft grey-green foliage and unusually dense indigo-blue flower spikes held on dark stems from late spring through summer.
water: Low once established; water during establishment and severe drought.
soil: Any well-drained soil, including chalky and relatively poor ground.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently wet or waterlogged soil, particularly during winter.
prune: Trim after the first flowering flush to maintain a compact habit and encourage repeat flowering.
resilience: Highly cold-hardy and drought resistant once established.
uses: Border fronts, path edging, rose underplanting, gravel gardens, wildlife planting, containers.

visual: Compact bushy perennial with narrow lance-shaped green leaves and abundant fully double golden-yellow pompon-like flowers held just above the foliage.
water: Moderate; keep watered during prolonged dry spells while avoiding saturated soil.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained or well-drained soil.
prune: Deadhead regularly for continuous flowering and cut old growth back in late autumn or winter.
hardinessNote: −15 to −10°C · hardy in most UK gardens with good drainage.
resilience: Good summer heat tolerance but winter survival is best in freely drained soil.
uses: Sunny borders, patio containers, cottage gardens, pollinator planting, edging.
